_doc: The events lane: how the studio reads public.analytics_sessions and public.analytics_events. Michi-maker and tcgscan-app share project piikwvntldytjejxmcla (migration 20260805100000_analytics_events.sql, authenticated-only RLS: guests are minted anon auth users). Doggle and pickleague each carry their OWN spine on their own project (doggle db/migrations/0377_analytics_events.sql, pickleague supabase/migration_add_analytics_events.sql) with nullable user_id + anon-role inserts, because their public pages are browsed signed-out: an identity-less visit is a real visit, grouped by device_id into a 'visitor'. Per-app projectRef below routes each app to its project; per-app `profile` maps that project's profiles name columns. Nothing here is queried by the apps themselves; this is read-only interpretation.
_campaignsDoc: The print/QR lane (scripts/campaigns.mjs) reads the same two tables through the same app->project map, so its config lives here rather than in a second file that could disagree about which project an app is on. `registry` is the path, relative to the repo root, to marketing-studio's list of codes that physically exist on paper — the join that makes a zero mean 'printed but never scanned' instead of 'we printed nothing'. `verificationPrefixes` are OUR OWN end-to-end proof scans: excluded from every headline the way our accounts are, and stated inline rather than dropped silently.
_appsDoc: Maps the `app` value the clients write to the studio's own app ids (config/apps.json), so exclusions and the DAU lane line up.
_taxonomyDoc: Every event name the two apps can emit, with a plain-English label and a stage. `stage` places the event on the acquisition -> activation -> engagement -> monetization spine; `milestone: true` marks the ones worth calling out on a journey timeline. Names seen in the data but missing here are reported as unrecognised rather than silently dropped, so instrumentation added upstream shows up as a prompt to update this file.
_plannedDoc: `planned: true` marks names registered ahead of implementation, specced in ../tcgscan/ANALYTICS-TRACKING-GAPS.md. Declaring them now means they are recognised the moment they land instead of arriving as unrecognised, and the coverage panel names them as unexercised rather than staying silent about the hole. `failure: true` marks events that record something going wrong, so the report can separate a drop-off caused by disinterest from one caused by a break.

collection.card_add.label: Added a card to a collection

collection.card_remove.label: Removed a card from a collection

taxonomy._asymmetryDoc: pro.offer_declined and search.no_results are michi-only, and that is correct rather than a half-done job. tcgscan's TrialCta renders on /plans alone, which has no dismissal, so there is no decline to record. tcgscan's search box lives inside the shared tcgscan-browse package and cannot report a result count without a package-level onEvent hook — tracked as gaps.tcgscan_search_blind, not as a missing call site.
taxonomy._capGatesDoc: A cap gate is the block a user hits when a tier limit stops them — 16 of 16 binder pages, 3 of 3 binders, the print gate. It is the moment upgrade intent is highest and, until these land, the one moment the stream cannot see. pro.offer_shown covers only the surfaces TrialCta itself renders; a gate that refuses an action without rendering that button emits nothing at all. `limit` MUST be the tier_caps limit_key verbatim so a gate joins to its cap without a lookup table.

_routesDoc: page.view routes that carry intent. `intent: pricing` marks the pages that constitute *demonstrated* PRO awareness — the strongest awareness signal available until an impression event exists (see gaps.trial_awareness).
_funnelsDoc: Ordered stages. A user counts at stage N only if they also reached every earlier stage, so the drop-off between rows is real. `match` is one of: event (any of `names`), route (a page.view whose route is in `routes`), or truth (a row in a ground-truth table — instrumentation-independent, so it also back-fills history from before tracking existed).
_funnelsNote: Shared-binder arrivals are deliberately NOT a funnel here. Answering it needs each binder's owner joined to the viewer, which this lane does not load - a route-only version would count owners opening their own binders as arrivals and quietly overstate the channel. The shares lane (scripts/shares.mjs, reports/shares.html) does it properly.

funnels.title: First-session activation
funnels.question: Do people who open the app ever do the core thing it is for?

funnels.title: Guest to account
funnels.question: Do anonymous guests ever convert into real accounts, and does the upgrade actually complete?

stages.label: Started as a guest
stages.note: Anyone whose session was stamped is_guest at the time. Not "is anonymous now" - that would drop everyone who converted out of the denominator of their own conversion funnel.

stages.label: Submitted the upgrade
stages.note: account.created fires when updateUser() returns, before the email is confirmed.

stages.label: Completed it (ground truth)
stages.note: auth.users.is_anonymous is false and the session carries upgraded_at. An upgrade whose email is never confirmed stays anonymous forever, so this is the only honest conversion count.

funnels.title: Visitor to account
funnels.question: Do signed-out visitors (QR scans included) become Doggle accounts?

funnels.title: Visitor to account
funnels.question: Do signed-out visitors (QR scans included) become Pickleague accounts?

_truthDoc: Ground-truth tables read alongside the event stream. These predate instrumentation, so they answer 'did it actually happen' for the whole history, not just since tracking went live. Used to cross-check the event stream and to catch under-counting.
_gapsDoc: Known holes between what the product does and what the stream records. Each is surfaced in the report next to the number it distorts, with `direction` saying which way the number is wrong. `status` tracks the fix: open (found, not yet specced), specced (written up in ../tcgscan/ANALYTICS-TRACKING-GAPS.md, awaiting implementation), landed (code is in the app repos but no event has been observed yet, so it is not proven), deferred (a decision was made not to do it, with the reason), fixed (observed firing). landed -> fixed is not a judgement call: the coverage panel detects a planned name appearing in the data and says so. Fixes land in the app repos, never here.

share_attribution.title: A binder open does not say what carried the visitor there
share_attribution.detail: CORRECTED 2026-08-06. This was first written up as blocking, on the reasoning that a shared-link arrival was unrecordable. That was wrong, and Brian caught it: page.view already carries props.route = /binder/<uuid>, so the binder id is in the data, and joining it to binders.owner_id separates a visitor from the owner reading their own binder. The whole channel is measurable from rows that already exist — see the shares lane, which needed no app change. What genuinely remains is narrower: the route cannot say HOW someone arrived, so a link from a friend and a click from /discover are identical. 'Arrived cold' (a binder open as the account's first ever action) is the proxy, since in-app browsing does not produce that.
share_attribution.direction: channel volume is measurable; only the referring surface is unknown
share_attribution.fix: not scheduled — deliberately. Distinguishing the two would need either a share token in the URL, which puts a tracking parameter in a link people paste to friends, or referrer capture, which is deferred for the privacy-copy reason under `referrer`. The share.* events registered in the taxonomy stay planned rather than specced: they would add sharer-side intent (made public, copied the link), which is a different question from arrivals and is not blocking anything.

landing_route_broken.title: landing_route was never written — the update was never sent
landing_route_broken.detail: Root cause found and fixed 2026-08-06 (michi-maker e07d2e1, tcgscan-app 7a979a8). Both apps wrote it through a bare `void supabase.from(...).update(...)`. supabase-js returns a PostgrestFilterBuilder, which is a LAZY thenable: it only issues its HTTP request when something calls .then(). `void builder` builds the query and drops it — no request, no error, nothing to catch. The sites that work (touchSession, and the guest-upgrade branch of resetSessionUser) all await, which is exactly why last_seen_at advanced normally while landing_route stayed null on all 91 sessions: same table, same policy, same session, different call shape. flushLastSeen had the identical defect, so the session_end fix was also silently doing nothing on the visibilitychange path. Not permissions: RLS grants authenticated UPDATE on auth.uid() = user_id, column-level UPDATE covers landing_route, and the guard trigger does not touch it.
landing_route_broken.direction: was: entry point unknown for every session, and session tails understated on tab-hide
landing_route_broken.fix: FIXED — verified in production 2026-08-08: 30 of the 58 sessions started in the preceding 48h carry a non-null landing_route, where every one of the 91 sessions before the fix was null. The remainder are sessions that never recorded a page.view (landing_route is backfilled from the first one), not a residual failure.

tcgscan_search_blind.title: TCGScan cannot see its own search queries
tcgscan_search_blind.detail: Free-typed search on tcgscan runs inside the shared tcgscan-browse package, which exposes no onEvent callback, so the app cannot observe a query or its result count. What it emits are proxies from outside the kit: card.search { kind: 'similar' } when find-similar is pressed, and card.open when a detail opens (documented at tcgscan-app/src/app/(tabs)/browse/index.tsx:169). michi has no such boundary and does emit search.no_results. Discovered 2026-08-06 while verifying the gap fixes; it is why search.no_results is registered for michi only rather than pending forever on tcgscan.
tcgscan_search_blind.direction: tcgscan search volume and zero-result rate are both unmeasurable; card.search understates real searching
tcgscan_search_blind.fix: add an onEvent callback to the tcgscan-browse package (search ran, result count), then consume it in tcgscan-app. Per tcgscan/AGENTS.md rule 3 that is a package release plus a commit-pin bump in each app — not a local interception, which the code comment there explicitly warns against.

trial_awareness.title: No impression event for the PRO trial offer
trial_awareness.detail: TrialCta renders the 'Start free 14-day PRO trial' button but emits nothing until it is pressed, and it returns null for anyone not eligible. The offer also appears outside /plans (michi's PrintPlaceholdersSheet), so a pricing page view neither implies nor is required for seeing it. Awareness is not measured, so the funnel's awareness stage reads zero — that zero is the gap, not a finding. Pricing-page views in the Pages table are the interim proxy, and they are a different and smaller set.
trial_awareness.direction: understates awareness — currently makes it unmeasurable
trial_awareness._whyStillZero: Verified 2026-08-06: the stage will keep reading zero even after pro.offer_shown ships, and that is a PRODUCT fact rather than an instrumentation one. useTrial returns early for guests (`if (!isSignedIn || !user) return`) and its state falls back to 'ineligible' when unresolved, so TrialCta renders null for every anonymous visitor. Guests are 3 of the 4 real users on michi. The one signed-in account (one michi account) has only ever visited /my-binders and two binder pages — never /plans, never a print gate. So nobody has been eligible AND in the right place. Do not read a persistent zero here as the fix having failed.
trial_awareness.fix: track('pro.offer_shown', { surface }) once per mount on the rendering path only (never the return-null path), plus pro.offer_declined on dismissal and a surface prop on trial.start. Both apps' components/monetization/TrialCta.tsx. Note this counts ELIGIBLE impressions only, which is the right denominator for offer conversion and the wrong one for audience awareness.
trial_awareness._landed: Verified 2026-08-07 17:25 UTC: pro.offer_shown fired twice on michi, once per surface — { surface: 'print_gate' } and { surface: 'plans' } — from a guest who had just converted in place. The awareness stage is measurable. It reads 1 impression / 0 starts, which is a rate with n=1, not yet a conversion rate.
trial_awareness._downgradedFromFixed: 2026-08-10, on an owner question the stream could not answer: 'was one michi account ever shown the PRO trial offer?' The event works; the GAP it was opened for does not close, for two reasons, and 'fixed' was hiding both.
trial_awareness._limit1_blindBeforeAug8: pro.offer_shown cannot be read as absent for anything before 2026-08-08. Until commit 0459e47 (2026-08-08 17:28 -0700) track() discarded every event fired before the auth store landed cachedUser — see trial_start_dropped, where a real entitlement-granting activation vanished that way. the account's whole visit (2026-08-05 23:23 to 2026-08-06 23:23 UTC) sits inside that window, and the emitter itself was only committed at 2026-08-05 23:13 UTC, ten minutes before their first session, with no verified deploy time. For that period, no impression is NOT no offer.
trial_awareness._limit2_wrongCorpus: The claim below in _whyStillZero — that one michi account 'never [hit] a print gate' — is now known to be the wrong question rather than a wrong answer. They hit a DIFFERENT gate, twice: both of their binders sit at exactly 16 of 16 pages, the free pagesPerBinder cap, and the second is titled 'part 2', which is the cap being worked around in plain sight. TrialCta never renders there, so pro.offer_shown is silent by construction, not by absence of intent. Measuring offer awareness while the cap gates that CREATE the intent emit nothing is measuring the wrong end of the funnel — tracked separately as cap_gates_blind.
trial_awareness._toClose: Ship cap_gates_blind, then re-verify awareness against a signed-in account that hits a cap AFTER 2026-08-08. Until an impression is observed for a user whose events were not droppable, this stays landed.

cap_gates_blind.title: Cap gates emit nothing, so upgrade intent is invisible
cap_gates_blind.detail: Every tier limit in tier_caps can stop a user — binders, pagesPerBinder, artUploads, cardScansPerMonth, collections, cardsPerCollection — and none of them emit an event when they do. The only monetization impression the stream has is pro.offer_shown, which fires from TrialCta; a gate that refuses an action without rendering that button is invisible. Hitting a cap is the highest-intent moment the product has, and it is the one moment the stream cannot see.
cap_gates_blind.direction: understates upgrade intent to exactly zero — every cap hit ever is unrecorded
cap_gates_blind._evidence: one michi account, a genuine external account (not excluded), created 2026-08-05 and active for one day. Ground truth: two binders, 'Ramochan binder idea' and 'part 2', BOTH at exactly 16 of 16 pages against the free pagesPerBinder cap of 16; 54 of 100 artworks; 2 of 3 binders. The stream for that account holds 11 page.view, 5 card.add, 4 session.start — and nothing about a limit. The workaround is legible in the title of the second binder and invisible in the events. Note the shape of the reasoning: the cap position came from product tables, the way trials do, which is why it survives the analytics drop window entirely.
cap_gates_blind.fix: Emit cap.gate_shown { limit, surface, tier, used, cap } once per gate impression, where `limit` is the tier_caps limit_key verbatim (pagesPerBinder, binders, artUploads, cardScansPerMonth, collections, cardsPerCollection) so it joins to the cap with no lookup table. Emit cap.gate_dismissed { limit, surface } when the user backs out without acting. Where a gate already renders TrialCta, pass the SAME surface string so cap.gate_shown, pro.offer_shown and trial.start share one attribution key and the gate-to-trial funnel is a join rather than a guess. Specced in ../tcgscan/ANALYTICS-CAP-GATES.md.
cap_gates_blind._denominatorNote: cap.gate_shown counts impressions of the block, which is the honest denominator for 'intent that met a wall'. It is NOT the count of users at a cap — an account can sit at 16 of 16 for weeks without touching the binder again, and that account is at the cap while emitting nothing. Read the two together: tier_caps position from the product tables for who IS capped, cap.gate_shown for who FELT it.
cap_gates_blind._landed: Shipped in BOTH apps on 2026-08-10, same day it was specced (michi commit 7e4f324). michi calls trackCapGate() directly at each gate; tcgscan routes them through lib/gate-prompt.ts. All six limit_keys are covered — binders (5 sites), pagesPerBinder (4), cardsPerCollection (3), collections (2), cardScansPerMonth (2), artUploads (1). The spec's two load-bearing details survived implementation: `limit` is the tier_caps limit_key verbatim, and `tier` is stamped at the gate rather than inferred later. The apps also added capCount() to normalise an unlimited cap, because JSON.stringify(Infinity) is null and would have landed indistinguishable from 'not captured' — a good catch that was not in the spec.
cap_gates_blind._whyNotFixed: Status stays LANDED, not fixed: as of 2026-08-10 analytics_events holds zero cap.gate_shown and zero cap.gate_dismissed rows. Every call site is unexercised, so nothing has proven the props arrive shaped as promised. To close it, hit a real cap on a signed-in account and confirm one row per gate with limit/surface/tier/used/cap populated — the verification steps are in ../tcgscan/ANALYTICS-CAP-GATES.md. Do not mark this fixed on the strength of the code reading correctly; that is exactly the mistake trial_awareness made.
cap_gates_blind._blockedBy: Verify AFTER the browse.tsx capacity bug is fixed (see the same work order). michi-maker/src/app/browse.tsx computes capacity as pagesPerBinder * 9, but a page is rows x cols and production holds 4x4, 3x4 and 2x2 pages — 15 of 330 are not 9 slots. Until that is corrected, `used` and `cap` on a gate emitted from browse inherit the error and would record the bug as if it were the user's behaviour.

trial_start_dropped.title: A real trial activation produced no trial.start event
trial_start_dropped.detail: Found 2026-08-08 by activating a trial by hand on an owner account. Ground truth recorded it — public.pro_trials gained a row and entitlements a 14-day tier_pro grant, both stamped 23:33:09.484Z — but analytics_events has no trial.start, and has never had one. The call site is not missing: michi-maker/src/components/monetization/TrialCta.tsx:61 calls track('trial.start', { surface }) immediately after the RPC resolves, and its catch would have emitted trial.start_failed had the RPC thrown. Neither appeared. The cause is the guard at michi-maker/src/lib/analytics.ts:385 — `if (!supabase || !cachedUser) return;` — which discards an event when the analytics module has not yet been handed the auth identity by resetSessionUser(). Corroborated by the clock: michi's analytics_sessions row for that user was not created until 23:33:31.262Z, 21.8 seconds AFTER the grant, so no session and no cachedUser existed at the moment of the click. Every event emitted in that window is lost with no error and no counter.
trial_start_dropped.direction: understates trial starts, and silently — the surface attribution just added by trial_awareness cannot be joined to an activation, so offer-to-start conversion stays unmeasurable even though both ends now exist
trial_start_dropped._whyItMatters: This is the exact failure the house rule about ground truth is for. The trial is not missing from the studio, because trials are read from pro_trials rather than the stream. Any metric that had trusted the event stream alone would have reported zero trials on a day one was actually started.
trial_start_dropped.fix: Preferred: emit from the start_pro_trial RPC server-side, which cannot be lost to a bootstrap race, a crash, or a blocked request — the comment at TrialCta.tsx:59 already names this as the more authoritative option. Cheaper alternative: buffer events emitted while cachedUser is null and flush on resetSessionUser(), rather than dropping them. Either way the drop should stop being silent — a swallowed analytics failure is correct, an unrecorded one that nothing counts is not. Specced in ../tcgscan/ANALYTICS-TRIAL-START-DROPPED.md.

guest_upgrade.title: A guest session is rewritten to look like it never was one
guest_upgrade.detail: The conversion event itself DOES exist: both apps emit account.created with props.via = 'guest_upgrade' (michi store/auth.tsx:309,348; tcgscan store/auth.tsx:198,266,283). What is lost is the session. resetSessionUser() patches analytics_sessions.is_guest in place when a guest signs up mid-session, so the row retroactively claims it was always an account. Sessions cannot be split into 'started as guest' and 'started signed in', and the session-level conversion rate is unrecoverable.
guest_upgrade.direction: guest-started sessions are undercounted; the conversion count itself is correct
guest_upgrade.fix: stop mutating is_guest — make it mean 'started as a guest' and add an upgraded_at column set at the transition, guarded by a trigger so a future client cannot regress it.
guest_upgrade._fixed: Proven by the first real conversion, 2026-08-07 17:24:58.845Z on michi — the only one that has ever happened, so this went from unexercised to verified on a sample of one. The session kept is_guest = true AND carries upgraded_at, and across all 181 sessions there are zero rows where upgraded_at is set but is_guest is false, which is the contradiction the old in-place rewrite produced. account.created followed 229ms later with via = 'guest_upgrade'. The whole pre-signup journey — /plans, /learn, a binder created while still a guest — stayed joined to the same uid.

session_end.title: Session length is a floor, not a duration
session_end.detail: last_seen_at is bumped opportunistically and throttled to 60s, and only when an event fires. There is no unload/background hook, so a session that ends after a long read records the timestamp of its last tracked action instead. Every duration is an underestimate, and single-event sessions read as zero seconds.
session_end.fix: flush a last_seen_at write on web 'visibilitychange'/'pagehide' and on RN AppState 'background'.

no_error_events.title: Nothing records failure
no_error_events.detail: No event marks a failed scan, a rejected CSV, a search with no results, or a checkout that errored. Every funnel measures only the happy path, so a stage that drops off cannot be distinguished between 'lost interest' and 'it broke'.
no_error_events.direction: hides the reason for every drop-off
no_error_events.fix: track('<feature>.failed', { reason }) on the error branches that already exist.

props_thin.title: A handful of events carry no props
props_thin.detail: Assessed against the code, not the recorded rows — the sample in the database is small enough to be misleading. Most call sites are already well instrumented: card.search carries kind, scan.capture carries mode and cards, csv.import carries cards, card.add carries source and count, account.created carries via, binder.add carries isDemo. The bare ones are demo.print, demo.tricolor_search, demo.csv_import, card.open, trial.start and the four collection.* events, so 'which demo precedes a signup' and 'which surface sold the trial' cannot be segmented.
props_thin.direction: limits segmentation on those events only; biases no count
props_thin.fix: add a small props object at those call sites; ids and counts only, per the no-PII rule in lib/analytics.ts.

referrer.title: No acquisition source
referrer.detail: Nothing records how a session arrived — no referrer, no UTM capture. Marketing spend cannot be attributed to activation or trials. DEFERRED by Brian on 2026-08-06, for a real reason rather than as a backlog punt: michi-maker/src/app/legal/privacy.tsx promises first-party records of 'which pages you open and product actions', and referrer/UTM are neither. Capturing them means changing that disclosure first, in both apps.
referrer.fix: not scheduled. When picked up: nullable referrer/utm_source/utm_medium/utm_campaign on analytics_sessions, web only, referrer stripped to origin + pathname CLIENT-SIDE so another site's query string cannot carry PII into our database — and the privacy copy updated in the same change.

upgrade_unconfirmed.title: account.created counts submitted upgrades, not completed ones
upgrade_unconfirmed.detail: Both apps fire account.created {via:'guest_upgrade'} the moment updateUser() returns, which is before the email is confirmed. An upgrade whose email is never confirmed leaves auth.users.is_anonymous = true forever - the person stays a guest and keeps their guest caps, while the stream says they made an account. On 2026-08-11, 4 users had fired the event and only 2 had confirmed: the event overstates completed conversion by 2x.
upgrade_unconfirmed.direction: conversion is overstated; the guest population is understated by the same people
upgrade_unconfirmed.fix: emit a second event on confirmation (auth.confirmed, or account.created {via:'guest_upgrade_confirmed'}) so submit and complete are separable in the stream. Until then the funnel reads completion from ground truth (auth.users.is_anonymous + analytics_sessions.upgraded_at), which is why that stage is labelled as such.
upgrade_unconfirmed._workaround: The signup funnel carries a fourth stage, match:"converted", read from ground truth rather than the stream. It is correct today but it cannot see WHEN someone confirmed, only that they have - so confirmation lag and confirm-after-window are both invisible.
upgrade_unconfirmed._evidence: Measured 2026-08-11: 4 users had fired account.created with via=guest_upgrade; 2 had confirmed (is_anonymous false), 2 had email null / email_confirmed_at null and were still anonymous. Names live in the gitignored roster, not here.

guest_device_churn.title: A guest who clears storage becomes a new person
guest_device_churn.detail: analytics_sessions has no device column, so identity for an anonymous user is only as durable as the Supabase session in storage. A reload keeps the same anon uid (persistence works - 5 michi anon uids span multiple days, one has 10 sessions), but cleared site data, incognito, a second browser or a reinstall mints a fresh uid with no join key to the old one. Guest counts are therefore an upper bound on guest PEOPLE.
guest_device_churn.direction: guest people are overstated; every rate with guests in the denominator is understated
guest_device_churn.fix: add analytics_sessions.device_id - a random opaque UUID generated once at first launch, persisted in localStorage/AsyncStorage, never regenerated on sign-out or upgrade. Specced in ../tcgscan/ANALYTICS-GUEST-DEVICE-ID.md.
guest_device_churn._notIpBased: Deliberately NOT solved with IP + user agent. One IP+UA pair holds 330 distinct anonymous uids on this project, another 144, another 58 - behind NAT that key is a building, not a person. Stitching on it would merge strangers and would also put location data into a join.
guest_device_churn._size: Measured 2026-08-11: of 115 anon uids created since instrumentation, the two largest device clusters (52 and 7 uids) are both on EXCLUDED dev IPs - the churn is almost entirely ours. Among real external traffic the largest cluster is 2.
guest_device_churn._forwardOnly: Cannot recover recorded history. The 45 michi guests in the 30d window will always be 45 uids.

qr_campaign_capture.title: Campaign codes ride on landing_route and account.created
qr_campaign_capture.detail: The emitters keep an allowlisted ?code/utm_* query on the first page.view (stored in landing_route) and merge the code into account.created props; all four apps landed the change 2026-08-13. Verified end-to-end against real rows in dev the same day: a fresh-context scan wrote landing_route='/welcome?code=...' plus device_id on michi, and 'Landing?code=...' plus the heartbeat/claim RPCs on doggle (the claim exercised as an authenticated JWT and reverted). Two bugs were found and fixed on the way: the fresh-visitor buffer wipe and the RLS select-gating no-op. What remains unproven is only production: the app code must deploy, and a printed code must be scanned for real.
qr_campaign_capture.direction: until a real scan lands, a zero in the campaigns panel means 'not verified end-to-end', not 'the card show produced nothing'.
qr_campaign_capture.fix: Deploy the app changes (migrations are already applied), then scan a printed code against production and confirm the session row carries code=<campaign>; then mark fixed.

anon_visitor_exclusions.title: Signed-out visits cannot be excluded
anon_visitor_exclusions.detail: Exclusions key on auth identity: email/uid always, IPs only for anonymous AUTH users. Doggle and pickleague visitor sessions have no auth user at all, so our own signed-out browsing counts as real traffic in their behavioural numbers. Signed-in dev traffic is still excluded normally, and michi/tcgscan are unaffected (their guests are anon auth users, IP exclusion applies).
anon_visitor_exclusions.direction: doggle/pickleague visitor counts are overstated by however much we browse our own public pages signed out.
anon_visitor_exclusions.fix: Either add a device_id exclusion list once dev devices are known, or browse the public pages signed in. Until then read visitor spikes next to the deploy/QA calendar.

doggle_oauth_signup_untracked.title: Doggle OAuth signups fire no account.created
doggle_oauth_signup_untracked.detail: account.created fires from the email/phone signUp wrappers in doggle's data/auth.ts. An OAuth (Google/Apple) signup never passes through them, so it emits only auth.login plus the session claim (upgraded_at). The doggle signup funnel stage carries this caveat.
doggle_oauth_signup_untracked.direction: doggle signups are undercounted by the OAuth share; the 'signed in on that visit' stage is the honest ceiling.
doggle_oauth_signup_untracked.fix: Fire account.created from the OAuth return path when the auth user was created moments before, mirroring michi's handling of the same ambiguity.

guestDepth._why: Which events count as a guest having BUILT something rather than merely browsed. Kept here so the activation bar is a config question, not a code one.
